diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Although Theorem~\ref{thm:dimfree_lip_velocity} is stated and proved in finite dimensions in \cite{meng2025pathway},
its Lipschitz bound involves constants that are independent of the ambient dimension.
We therefore interpret it as a function-space stability statement.

We work in a function-space regime: let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space with norm
$\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{H}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space with trace-class $C$, but the source gives no proof; the only support is a citation whose proof, by the paper's own remark, "is stated and proved in finite dimensions in \cite{meng2025pathway}". Dimension-free constants in finite dimensions do not yield the infinite-dimensional statement: existence, measurability, and Lipschitz regularity of the Föllmer velocity on $\mathcal{H}$ (and a finite-dimensional approximation/limit argument) are never established, so the theorem is unsupported as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the cited result with the scope in which it is actually proved (finite-dimensional, dimension-free constants) and either supply a genuine infinite-dimensional argument (e.g., finite-dimensional approximation plus tightness/consistency of the Föllmer velocity on $\mathcal{H}$) or explicitly downgrade the main-text one-step transport regularity claim to a per-discretization statement.
issues.overall_effect: The only formal support for 'trace-class reference implies a globally Lipschitz one-step transport in function space' is unproven; lem:avg_velocity_lipschitz (which assumes this theorem), cor:exists_lipschitz_onestep, the main-text Theorem thm:lipschitz_onestep_main, and the abstract/conclusion claims of established function-space Lipschitz regularity all become unreliable. The white-vs-trace-class singularity proposition is independent and unaffected.
issues.title: Function-space Lipschitz velocity theorem rests on a finite-dimensional citation
issues.why_classification: A contained resolution exists (finite-dimensional restatement with dimension-free constants, or a scoped weakening), preserving the design rationale and all experiments, but it withdraws the advertised infinite-dimensional guarantee and needs more than a routine local edit, so it exceeds minor without requiring new global architecture: moderate.

issues.failure_explanation: The first inequality treats the average velocity as a time-average of $v(\cdot,\tau)$ at a common spatial point, but by its definition $w(z;r,t)=\frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t v(z_\tau,\tau)d\tau$ averages $v$ along the flow trajectory through $z$, i.e. $w(z;0,1)=z-\varphi_{0\leftarrow 1}(z)$ with $\varphi$ the backward flow map. Its Lipschitz constant is governed by the derivative of the flow map, not by the average of $\mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))$. Counterexample: $v(\tau,z)=L_0\tau\sin z$ on $\mathbb{R}$ has $\mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))=L_0\tau$, yet $w(z;0,1)=z-\varphi_{0\leftarrow 1}(z)$ has $|w'(\pi)|=e^{L_0/2}-1>L_0/2$, and the one-step map $\mathcal{T}=\varphi_{0\leftarrow 1}$ has $\mathrm{Lip}(\mathcal{T})\ge e^{L_0/2}>1+L_0/2$. Hence the stated bounds in the lemma and corollary are false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the averaging step with a Gronwall estimate on the variational equation of the flow: $\mathrm{Lip}(\varphi_{0\leftarrow 1})\le\exp(\int_0^1\mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))d\tau)\le e^{L_0/2}$, so $\mathrm{Lip}(\mathcal{T})\le e^{L_0/2}$ and $\mathrm{Lip}(w(\cdot;r,t))\le(1+e^{L_0(t^2-r^2)/2})/(t-r)$, and restate the lemma and corollary with these corrected constants.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative Lipschitz bounds $\mathrm{Lip}(w(\cdot;0,1))\le L_0/2$ and $\mathrm{Lip}(\mathcal{T})\le 1+L_0/2$ (and their informal restatement in the main text) are unsupported and in general false; only the qualitative existence of a globally Lipschitz one-step map survives, with a larger constant.
issues.title: False averaging inequality in the Lipschitz bound for the Mean-Flow average velocity
issues.why_classification: The stated constant is false (counterexample above), so the bound must be withdrawn and re-derived via a contained but nontrivial standard argument (Gronwall on the flow map); the guarantee type (globally Lipschitz one-step map, dimension-free constant) survives with a comparable constant, so the loss is limited: moderate, not minor, not serious.
